content.title: About
content.content: Nonfat cereals and granola bars are dry grain products made without added fats. They typically contain whole grains, bran, dried fruit, sweeteners, and added vitamins and minerals for enrichment. The product is aimed at people who monitor fat intake but still want energy and nutrients from grains.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nonfat cereals are popular in sports nutrition because they are quickly digested and provide rapid energy.
Fat‑free granola bars may contain more sugar to compensate for the lack of flavor, so checking the ingredient list is important.
The “fat‑free” process usually removes oil from the grains and replaces it with dry ingredients rather than eliminating all lipids.
In many countries these products must be labeled as “low‑calorie” or “low‑fat.”
Fiber content in nonfat cereals is often higher than in their full‑fat counterparts due to the use of bran.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs provide sustained satiety and a stable blood‑glucose level.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2, B3 and folate support metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps normalize cholesterol, and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Suitable for low‑fat diets and for individuals controlling calorie intake.

items.title: Fortified with minerals
items.content: Often enriched with iron, zinc and magnesium, which are essential for blood formation and muscle function.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: To replace flavor lost without fat, many products add significant amounts of sugar or syrups, raising the glycemic index.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain nuts, soy protein, gluten, or dried fruit—check the label if you have allergies.

items.title: Lack of healthy fats
items.content: Absence of fats can reduce absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), which should be obtained from other sources.

items.title: Potential additives
items.content: Some versions contain artificial sweeteners, flavors or preservatives that may be undesirable for sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cereals can be poured over milk, kefir or plant‑based drinks and topped with fresh berries. Granola bars are convenient for on‑the‑go snacks; they can be broken up and added to yogurt or oatmeal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed package. After opening, keep the product in an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crunch.
